summary:
Camera, round 10: both items of the assignment are fixed in src/js/50-camera.js; src/css/50-camera.css is unchanged (byte for byte the base9m copy). Started 06:28, last check 06:55.

1) t9-camera-1: a pinch that pushes on against a zoom limit now shows the same note as the wheel and the buttons (3D nearest and farthest, 2D closest and widest, row and column wording). It waits until the pinch has asked for a tenth more than the limit allows, so two fingers that only slide the picture at a limit do not trigger it.

2) solids-7, remaining part: the Kleinian start view with a trap solid on now looks at the picture as Reset view does. Finding: in the tester's case the program WAS ready at the click (pick() saw the picture in the same call); the start view simply never looked. The look is now left waiting by resetCam() and runs before the next frame when the picture can be seen, or on the first frame after its program is ready. It takes place only while the camera is exactly as the start view left it (no pointer down, no key, no easing, same limits, same camera kind, still Kleinian); otherwise it is dropped for good, so nothing moves after the user has started to drag.

What did not change (measured): 735 values (boxes of all the picture's controls, cover, hints, classes, cameras and 2D views for the opening view, the three start views, 2D view, fly, Reset view) at 1400x950, 1024x768 and 375x812 are identical between dist/v9m.html and dist/r10-camera.html. Smoke test tools/smoke-v9m.json on the final page: 52 steps, exit 0, no console errors.

Measured: everything in the evidence fields (headless Chrome, real mouse and emulated touch through the tester's rig). Only reasoned: behaviour on a slow machine or a real phone, the choice of a tenth as the pinch threshold, and the fallback of camCanSee() to renderIdle() (never taken in a run). Not re-run: the tester's full real.py and views.py suites (their page name is fixed to dist/v8.html); my driver repeats the parts that concern these two items.

fixed.what: camPinch() now reports what the fingers asked for and what the limits allowed to a new camPinchPast(); once a pinch has asked for a tenth more than a limit allows (CAM_PINCH_PAST, log scale) the limit note is shown through camStopNote(end), the same sentence and the same left end / right end wording that camZoomTo() uses (that code was moved into camStopNote unchanged). Moving back inside the limits pays the amount off; lifting a finger clears it. Fly mode has no limit and no note.
fixed.evidence: Reproduced first on dist/v9m.html from a state with no note on show (python out/r10/camera/drive.py pinch dist/v9m.html, out/r10/camera/pinch-v9m.log: 17 pass, 4 fail): pinch at nearest limit 0.5 -> [0.5, ""], at farthest 20 -> [20, ""], 2D closest zoom 1 -> [1, ""], slider as a column -> "". Same script on dist/r10-camera.html (out/r10/camera/pinch-r10.log: 21 pass, 0 fail): [0.5, "This is the nearest the zoom may go. The box at the left end of the slider sets that limit."]; [20, "This is the farthest the zoom may go. The box at the right end of the slider sets that limit."]; 2D: [1, "This is the closest the zoom may go. The box at the left end of the slider sets that limit. Below 0.0005 the picture loses sharpness."]; phone on its side: "...The box at the top of the slider sets that limit." The + button at the same limit gives the identical sentence. No note for: a pinch inside the limits (5.2 -> 2.6), a pinch from 0.52 asking 2% past the limit, two fingers sliding at the limit with the spread wobbling by 2 px, a pinch while flying. The note goes away after 6 s. Pictures looked at at full size: out/r10/camera/v9m-pinch-near-window.png (no note) against out/r10/camera/r10-camera-pinch-near-window.png and r10-camera-pinch-far-window.png (note readable at the lower left of the picture, above the Arcball / Fly switch). No console errors.

fixed.id: solids-7 (remaining part: Kleinian start view with a trap solid)
fixed.what: resetCam() now leaves a look waiting (camLookLater) when the mode is Kleinian, the 3D picture is on show, a trap is the solid or is added to it, and the camera was not given by the caller. camLookTick() runs first on a 0 ms timer (after the caller has finished changing settings, before the next frame), then on every frame until pick() can see the picture (camCanSee), for at most 15 s; it then runs the existing camStepBack(). The look is dropped for good if anything about the camera differs from what the start view left (yaw, pitch, distance, target, camera kind, zoom limits, mode) or a pointer is down, a key is held, a zoom is easing or the slider is held. resetView() behaves as before when the picture can be seen; pressed while the picture is being prepared, the waiting look now does its job. Mandelbrot and Julia start views and cameras given by examples are untouched.
fixed.evidence: Reproduced first on dist/v9m.html (python out/r10/camera/drive.py kstart dist/v9m.html, out/r10/camera/kstart-v9m.log): ring trap is the solid, thickness 0.2, mode away and back: camera 7, 40 frame probes hit (bottom 24, left 16), no note; Reset view 9.913. On dist/r10-camera.html (out/r10/camera/kstart-r10.log, 11 pass, 0 fail): same steps give 9.913 with 0 frame probes, and the frame trace reads [[0, 5.256], [80, 9.913]], so 7 was never on show; Reset view after it stays 9.913. Program not prepared at the click (fresh page, warm-up off; at the click renderIdle false and pick sees nothing): pick could see after 40 ms, camera 7 -> 9.913 at 160 ms, 0 frame probes. Same cold start with a 50 px drag begun straight after the click: yaw -0.05 (turned by the drag), distance 7, identical 2 s later and after release. A press held 2.5 s on the picture: distance 7 throughout and after release. One wheel notch straight after the click: 6.25 (7 / 1.12), nothing stepped back. Reset view pressed straight after the click: 9.913, 0 probes. Example Rings in the lace (camera given): 7, unchanged a second later. No trap solid: 7. Pictures looked at at full size: out/r10/camera/v9m-k-2-start-thick0.2.png (green sheet cut by the lower left of the frame) against out/r10/camera/r10-camera-k-2-start-thick0.2.png and r10-camera-k-4-cold.png (whole solid inside the frame at 9.91). No console errors.

not_fixed.id: solids-7 (dials part, not in this round's assignment)
not_fixed.why: Typing a trap dial (thickness, radius, centre) still leaves the camera where it is and shows no word, so a Kleinian trap solid can still grow out of the frame until the user presses Reset view. Round 7 chose that dials do not move the camera, the round 10 brief gives the camera only the start view, and a camera that moves while a dial is typed would be a new behaviour, so I left it.
not_fixed.learned: Measured again on both pages: thickness 0.2 typed in Kleinian mode leaves the camera at 7 with 40 frame probes hit and no note; my change does not touch that path (typing the dial does not arm a look). If it is wanted later, the same waiting look (camLookLater) could be armed from a dial change, but it would move the camera without the user asking, which is why it was not done. Also left on purpose: if the 2D view is up when the mode changes to Kleinian, no look is armed and the 3D camera stands at 7 until Reset view; and the look probes the frame about every 30 px as in round 7, so a sliver can still slip through.

names_added: camHome() result gains the field given (true when the camera was used exactly as given)
resetCam(): drops any waiting look and may arm one (behaviour change, same signature)
resetView(): drops the waiting look when the picture can be seen (same signature)
needs_from_others: Joiner: take src/js/50-camera.js as a whole; src/css/50-camera.css needs no change (identical to base9m/css/50-camera.css). No id, label, class or public function changed; nothing new on window.squaringLab.

Engine engineer (src/js/40-render.js), for information only: camCanSee() in 50-camera.js reads sceneNow() and the map progs (an entry's state === 'ready'), the same test pick() makes. Both are asked for with typeof first. If either is renamed nothing breaks, but the camera falls back on renderIdle() and the Kleinian start view then stands back when the picture is finished instead of when it can first be seen (this fallback was reasoned, not run). Please keep the two names, or tell the joiner.

Page closing text (src/body.html): I searched it for 'pinch', 'Reset view', 'start view' and 'zoom limit' and found no sentence that my changes make untrue (only the button label and the two sentences about Show Figure 4 moving a zoom limit, which still hold). If the closing text or the list of known limits says anywhere that the Kleinian start view with a trap solid is cut until Reset view, or that a pinch at a zoom limit says nothing, those are no longer true. Suggested wording if a line is wanted: 'With a trap as the solid, the Kleinian start view stands back until the solid fits the picture. Typing a trap dial still leaves the camera where it is; Reset view frames the solid again.'
src/js/75-presets.js line 80 (comment only, carried over from round 7): 'hidden behind the zoom slider (Kleinian)' is out of date on a narrow stage; no code change needed.
risks: All touch evidence is headless Chrome with touch emulated through the debugging port, not real fingers. The pinch threshold of a tenth was chosen by reasoning: a very slow real pinch with jittery fingers may need a little more push before the note shows, and a two-finger slide whose spread drifts steadily by more than a tenth while resting on a limit will show the note.

The Kleinian start view with a trap solid on now differs from Version 9 by design (7 becomes what Reset view gives, here 9.913; at most twice the distance, or the existing 'runs out of the picture' note). Each such start view costs one look of about 100 pick() calls on the shared GPU (round 7 measured 60 to 270 ms for it; not timed again this round).

When the Kleinian program has to be prepared after the click, the picture can show the camera at 7 as a preview for a frame or two before it stands back, because the renderer draws its first preview in the same call that finds the program ready. Measured here only on a fast compile: ready 40 ms after the click, camera moved at 160 ms. On a slow machine the wait is longer; the look is given up after 15 s.
camCanSee() depends on two names of 40-render.js that are not in the contract (sceneNow, progs). Guarded, with a fallback to renderIdle() that was never exercised in a run.

The tester's own suites (out/t9/camera/real.py desk and phone, views.py resets) were not re-run against my page because their page name is fixed to dist/v8.html; my driver out/r10/camera/drive.py repeats the pinch, the Kleinian start view and the boxes and start views at three sizes. The desktop wheel, keys, fly camera, slider and limit boxes were not driven again; they are covered only by the unchanged-values comparison and by the smoke test (52 steps, exit 0, no console errors).
The smoke test was run once on the final page; the other engineers were using the GPU at the same time, so timings in my logs are from a shared machine.
